text:
Andrew Peeke arrived in Utah from Boston and has already matched more than half of last season's point total: 8 points through 22 games, after 14 in 77 last year. The Hockey News calls him "Utah's Professional Pest," and his minutes have grown to 19.9 a night over the last ten games, more than three above his usual.

Our read is split. His own scoring is running hot: 1.21 points per 60 against a talent range centred near 0.77, and 11.1% shooting against a range near 6.5%. That part is likely to cool. At the same time, the Mammoth have scored 9.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which our numbers flag as due to swing back. The team's 56% share of expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him out there is respectable.

The old weakness is still the thing to watch. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season had only 24% of his exits keeping possession, so pay attention when a forecheck leans on him. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level in 2025-26.
